subject: humanities
passage: English spelling often preserves pronunciations that disappeared centuries ago. The k in "knight" and the gh in "night" were once sounded, as similar letters still are in related German words, but by the time spellings began to settle after the arrival of printing, speech had moved on while the written forms largely stayed put. The result is an orthography that is less irrational than ______: a record of earlier speech, frozen at a moment when the spoken language was already shifting beneath it.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

explanation.why: "Less irrational than ______" means the blank offers a better description than "irrational." The colon explains it: spelling is "a record of earlier speech, frozen" in place. "Fossilized" means preserved in an old form after the living thing has changed.
explanation.A: Correct. Like a fossil, English spelling preserves the shape of something that has since changed: the way words were once pronounced.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Arbitrary" is close in meaning to "irrational," the very description the text says is less accurate; the text explains a historical reason for the spellings.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Provisional" means temporary and open to change, but the text says the written forms "stayed put" and were "frozen."
explanation.D: Incorrect. A phonetic spelling matches current pronunciation, but the text says English spelling records pronunciations that "disappeared centuries ago."
